title: Schedule the Meeting Before Completing the Work
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership offers a simple scheduling habit: before a project starts, work out which meetings or calls it will need and book them all up front. The post argues that waiting to schedule leaves work idle while calendars are coordinated, and with several attendees a workable time may be weeks away. A second benefit is that the booked meetings become built-in deadlines and milestones, since an upcoming call pushes people to finish work. The author concedes that the advice seems obvious yet is routinely overlooked because busy people resist thinking about future meetings. The recommendation is to prearrange the full set of meetings now to keep momentum.

quotes: People are incredibly busy. So much so that scheduling meetings and calls is becoming increasingly difficult.
When you delay, the work or project sits idle while the schedules are coordinated. Valuable time is lost and wasted.
The better call is to think through what meetings or calls the project or team will require before the work begins. Schedule all of them, or as many as possible, now.

Scheduling the set of meetings before completing the work saves valuable time and keeps the momentum for the project going. An additional advantage to this approach makes it even more appealing. Once the meetings or calls are on the books, those involved can use them as deadlines or milestones for work completion.
In a competitive and fast-paced world, believing you can quickly arrange for a meeting of the minds is often a fantasy. People are booked, and their calendars are nearly impossible to move around.
So, make the small call and prearrange for all the upcoming meetings now. You won’t regret it.
